crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Credit Scoring with Alternative Data
children.blurb: Credit scoring with alternative data extends traditional credit assessment beyond bureau files and application data to sources such as rental payments, utility bills, telecom records, bank transaction flows, e-commerce activity, and small business accounting or point-of-sale data.

children.name: Covenant Extraction
children.blurb: Covenant extraction is the use of natural language processing and machine learning to identify, classify, and structure the contractual terms in bond indentures and loan agreements.

children.name: Predicting Distress and Default
children.blurb: Predicting distress and default covers models that estimate the probability a corporate or sovereign borrower will miss payments, enter bankruptcy, or restructure, using financial statements, market prices, news, and alternative data.

children.name: Modelling the Yield Curve
children.blurb: Yield curve modelling in fixed income and credit risk concerns the term structure of interest rates across maturities, from overnight to long dated government and credit instruments.

children.name: Stress Testing Structured Credit
children.blurb: Stress testing structured credit means assessing how tranches of securitized products such as CLOs, ABS, RMBS, and CMBS would perform under severe economic and market shocks, including defaults, prepayments, spread widening, and rating migration.

sections.body: Fixed income and credit risk is the part of AI economics that applies machine learning to debt instruments, loan documents, and borrower behaviour. In practice, models now score borrowers using rent, utility, and transaction records rather than only credit bureau files. Software reads loan agreements to pull out covenants, the rules that protect lenders. Other systems flag companies that may miss payments or file for bankruptcy. Work also covers fitting the yield curve from bond prices and running stress tests on bundles of loans such as mortgage or collateralised debt securities.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has made real progress on narrow, repetitive tasks. Covenant extraction is reliable for standard boilerplate language but still needs human review for unusual or negotiated clauses. Credit scoring with alternative data can widen access, yet it depends on data quality and raises questions about stability and fairness. Distress prediction works best over short horizons, and long range forecasts remain noisy with many false alarms. Yield curve models fit historical data well but do not reliably predict future rate moves. Stress testing structured credit is only as good as the assumptions about defaults and correlations, which are hard to estimate in calm periods.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking at borrower assessment would begin with Credit Scoring with Alternative Data, which shows how non traditional records feed risk models. Covenant Extraction then explains how the terms of a loan are turned into structured data for monitoring. Predicting Distress and Default connects those borrower and loan signals to early warning scores for missed payments or bankruptcy. Modelling the Yield Curve steps back to the interest rate environment that prices all fixed income. Stress Testing Structured Credit brings the pieces together by shocking a portfolio of loans under assumed downturns, using the outputs of the earlier pages.
